items.title: HAI fall conference recap: 'AI's Future Is Still a Choice'
items.summary_en: Stanford HAI recaps its fall conference, held at Stanford on Oct. 28, 2026. The event was organized around the tension between hope and fear about AI.
items.notes: hai.stanford.edu was not reachable by WebFetch (DNS blocked). Title, URL and date come from a web search snippet only; the page itself was not read. Date may be slightly off.

items.title: Study tracks AI hallucinations in four U.S. state courts
items.summary_en: Researchers built a benchmark from documented AI hallucination cases. They used it to calibrate detectors and track the rise of generative AI in four U.S. state courts.
items.notes: Search snippet only. No article-specific URL was available, so the news index is cited and no URL was invented. Date and details are unverified. The Orchestrator should have the article URL checked.

items.title: Computer-vision system monitors ICU patients for delirium
items.summary_en: Computer vision researchers developed a 24/7 video monitoring system. It tracks patient activity and helps clinicians spot subtle signs of delirium.
items.notes: Search snippet only. Generic index URL, no article URL found. Peer-review status unknown.

items.title: HAI selects 12 new Student Affinity Groups
items.summary_en: HAI announced 12 new student affinity groups. Topics include accessibility, healthcare and journalism.

items.title: Third AI100 report says AI has outrun expectations and governance
items.summary_en: The AI100 report is covered in a HAI piece titled 'The World Has Changed'. According to the snippet, it describes a technology that has outrun both expectations and governance.
